title: The Battle of Hastings
description: October 1066. William of Normandy's invasion army faces King Harold's Anglo-Saxon shield wall on Senlac Hill. The player commands the Norman force and must break the shield wall through feigned retreats and combined cavalry-archer assaults before nightfall ends the battle.

issues_found: Both players are set to RANDOM civilization, so Norman and Anglo-Saxon architecture, unit bonuses and visual identity are left to chance — Franks/Britons were available and avoidable error.

4,800 TREE_OAK objects blanket a 120x120 map; Senlac Hill was an open ridge with a marshy bottom and cleared slopes, not dense forest, and heavy woods make the cavalry-versus-shield-wall action the brief describes impossible to stage.

Random-map economic furniture (10 gold mines, 8 stone mines, 16 forage bushes, 12 sheep, 8 deer) plus Town Centers, Blacksmith, Archery Range, Stable, Barracks and Monastery frame a base-building match rather than a single-day pitched battle; no army in 1066 was building a monastery on the field.
Player 2 receives 2 Guard Towers, and both sides a Town Center — no fortifications existed on Senlac Hill; Harold's strength was the unfortified shield wall itself.
Harold is represented by the KING unit, a militarily inert object, whereas Harold fought and died in the line; a renamed Champion or Teutonic Knight would have been a truer stand-in.

The 'Feigned Retreat Draws the Housecarls' trigger only prints text — no housecarls actually break formation or change ownership/stance, so the battle's decisive tactic is asserted rather than modelled.

Both players are set to RANDOM civilization, so Norman (Frankish) and Anglo-Saxon (Briton/Teuton) architecture, unit bonuses and tech are left to chance — an entirely avoidable error since the engine offers appropriate civs

4,800 oak trees on a 120x120 map buries Senlac Hill in dense forest; the battle was fought on an open ridge and slope above marshy ground, and heavy woods also make the cavalry feigned-retreat manoeuvre the brief centres on physically awkward

Economic furniture inappropriate to a single-day pitched battle: 10 gold mines, 8 stone mines, 16 forage bushes, sheep and deer, plus a Town Center, Barracks, Stable, Archery Range and Blacksmith for the Normans and a Town Center and Monastery for Harold — Hastings involved no base-building on either side
Player 2's two Guard Towers give the Saxons stone fortification they did not possess; Harold's line was a shield wall of men only

The feigned-retreat turning point is only a DISPLAY_INSTRUCTIONS message fired by OBJECTS_IN_AREA — no Saxon units are actually made to break ranks and pursue, so the mechanic the brief promises is narrated rather than modelled
The Norman archers' opening volley, Harold's brothers Gyrth and Leofwine, and the Malfosse pursuit are absent
